project_name: Coronado Island Reliability Reinforcement Phase I
brief_description: New underground 69 kV line f rom Station B to North Island Metering.
objectives: Improve system reliability against the P1 contingencies of TL650 Station B – Coronado and TL655 Silvergate – Coronado which would overload the remaining line, and increase the load serving capability, driven by the additional US Navy load.
driver_detail: The US Navy submitted a load interconnection request to add 95 MVA of load at North Island Metering substation from 2023 to 2042, triggering P1 and P3 contingency overloads on TL650 Station B–Coronado and TL655 Silvergate–Coronado in the near term and long term. Load_growth: explicit 95 MVA new load from US Navy. Equip_aging: existing two 69 kV lines are undersized to serve this additional load under contingency conditions. Phase I builds a new underground 69 kV line from Station B to North Island Metering sufficient for 2028–2034.
load_growth_evidence: The US Navy submitted a load interconnection request to SDG&E that will add 95 MVA of load at North Island Metering substation from 2023 to 2042. P1 and P3 contingency overloads were observed in the near term and long term planning horizons driven by this additional load.
alternatives_rejected: • Build a new underground 69 kV line f rom Bay Boulevard to North Island Metering with a cost of $300 to $400 million and an in-service date of 2032. • Installation of energy storage at Coronado Island, but this alternative is not appropriate due to energy storage charging limitations. • Addition of flow control devices is not applicable since Coronado Island load is radial and only served by two 69 kV lines. • RAS is not suitable per ISO RAS Guidelines where involuntary load tripping is not allowed due to critical US Navy load. May 30, 2025

driver_detail: After Phase I adds a third 69 kV line, P1 contingency overloads on TL655 Silvergate–Coronado (starting 2035) and TL650 Station B–Coronado (starting 2040) remain due to the additional US Navy load. load_growth_evidence: All P1 contingency overloads in Phase II are 'driven by the additional US Navy load' of 95 MVA at North Island Metering substation, same as Phase I.
alternatives_rejected: • Addition of series reactors/flow control devices to TL650 and TL655 or a series capacitor/flow control device to the new 69 kV line to redistribute the power f low during P1 contingencies. This alternative is unf easible due to space limitations at existing Station B, Coronado, North Island Metering, and Silvergate substations and the lack of land to expand them. • Installation of energy storage at Coronado Island, but this alternative is not appropriate due to energy storage charging limitations. • RAS is not suitable per ISO RAS Guidelines where involuntary load tripping is not allowed due to critical US Navy load.

project_name: Tortilla 115kV Capacitor Replacement
brief_description: Replace the existing two (2) 14.4 MVAR 115 kV capacitors at the Tortilla 115/33 kV substation with two (2) new 28.8 MVAR 115 kV capacitors. The capacitor replacement will complement the Kramer-Coolwater 115 kV line looping into the Tortilla 115 kV substation, which primarily addresses thermal overload concerns, while the capacitor project f ocuses on mitigating low voltage issues.
objectives: • To mitigate low voltage and voltage collapse issues in the NOL area under N-1 conditions resulting f rom various outages.
driver_detail: Low voltage and voltage collapse risk in the North of Lugo (NOL) area under contingency conditions. The report explicitly states: 'The decline in post-contingency voltage is primarily driven by the significant increase in load at Tortilla and Edwards substations.' Replacing existing 14.4 MVAR capacitors with 28.8 MVAR units at Tortilla 115/33 kV substation addresses the reactive power deficiency caused by load growth. This project complements the Kramer-Coolwater line loop which addresses thermal overloads.
load_growth_evidence: Report explicitly states: 'The decline in post-contingency voltage is primarily driven by the significant increase in load at Tortilla and Edwards substations.'
alternatives_rejected: • Looping the Kramer-Coolwater 115 kV line into the Tortilla 115 kV Substation was considered by itself. While this option mitigates thermal overloads and provides some additional VAR support, it does not fully resolve the low voltage issues expected in the coming years. • An 80MW Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) was considered to mitigate the low voltage and voltage collapse concerns. However, low voltages were identified when charging the large BESS in the 2029 Summer OP case, which would likely prohibit fully recharging the batteries during extended transmission contingency conditions. May 30, 2025

project_name: Kramer-Coolwater 115kV Line Looping into Tortilla 115kV Substation
brief_description: Utilize the existing Kramer-Coolwater 115 kV transmission line to loop in the Tortilla 115/33 kV substation via an approximate 11.5-mile double-circuit line extension and switchrack expansion at the Tortilla 115/33 kV substation.
objectives: To mitigate thermal overloads and reduce the risk of voltage collapse due to N1 loss of the Coolwater-SEGS-Tortilla, Kramer-Accelerate, or AccelerateTortilla 115 kV lines.
driver_detail: Thermal overloads and voltage collapse risk under N-1 line contingencies in the North of Lugo area. The report explicitly states: 'The decline in post-contingency voltage is primarily driven by the significant increase in load at Tortilla and Edwards substations.' The existing Kramer-Coolwater 115 kV line does not serve Tortilla directly—looping it in creates a new supply path (equip_aging: current network topology is insufficient for contingency conditions). The project both mitigates thermal overloads and reduces voltage collapse risk (voltage).
load_growth_evidence: Report explicitly states: 'The decline in post-contingency voltage is primarily driven by the significant increase in load at Tortilla and Edwards substations.' Load growth is the stated driver for both thermal and voltage concerns.
alternatives_rejected: • Constructing a new 11.4-mile 115 kV circuit f rom Coolwater to Tortilla (a double-circuit tower alongside the existing Coolwater-SEGS-Tortilla 115 kV line) was considered. However, this solution would result in Tortilla being supported by only three lines instead of four. Additional work at the Coolwater Substation would be required to accommodate the new line position, and the Coolwater-SEGS-Tortilla 115 kV line would f ace long outages during the construction phase. • An 80MW Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) was considered to mitigate thermal overloads and voltage collapse concerns. However, low voltages were identified when charging the large BESS in the 2029 Summer OP case, which would likely prohibit fully recharging the batteries during extended transmission contingency conditions. May 30, 2025

driver_detail: The long-term load forecast in the San Jose area increased from 2,100 MW (2021-2022 TPP) to ~3,400 MW base / ~4,200 MW sensitivity scenario in the 2024-2025 TPP. The previously approved two San Jose HVDC projects were re-scoped due to this load increase. This new 230 kV line (San Jose B to SVP NRS, ~7 miles) complements the HVDC re-scope by providing an additional path for the 1,000 MW HVDC injection and a backup 230 kV source during DC supply outage. Driven entirely by dramatic long-term load growth in the San Jose area.
load_growth_evidence: Long-term San Jose area load forecast increased from 2,100 MW in the 2021-2022 TPP to ~3,400 MW (base) and ~4,200 MW (sensitivity) in the 2024-2025 TPP—a 62-100% increase. The previously approved HVDC projects were re-scoped and this new line was added as a complement.
alternatives_rejected: • The alternative analysis was assessed in the San Jose area HVDC lines rescope assessment. Since this is a complementary component of the project, no alternatives were evaluated. May 30, 2025

project_name: South Bay Reinforcement Project
brief_description: Reconductor the 115 kV transmission lines and components to higher capacity: San Jose B – Trimble, Kief er – FMC,San Jose A – El Patio, Mountain View – Monta Vista, Whisman – Monta Vista, and Los Esteros – Metcalf 230 kV. Additionally, it includes the loop-in of the Los Esteros – Montague 115 kV line at Ringwood substation.
objectives: • To ensure enough transmission capacity and reliability in the South Bay to prevent the 115 kV system overloads due to the aggressive ramp-up in load trends ref lected in the current load f orecast • To reinf orce the most important 115 kV paths in the South Bay af ter the interconnection of the other bigger scope proposed projects for the area, such as the 500 kV line to Metcalf , the 500/230 kV transf ormer bank at this substation, the 1,000 HVDC line Metcalf – San Jose B, and the Newark – NRS, and NRS – San Jose B 230 kV lines.
driver_detail: Explicit aggressive load growth: the report's objectives state 'the aggressive ramp-up in load trends reflected in the current load forecast' as the primary cause of thermal violations in the South Bay 115 kV network. Previously approved projects (San Jose HVDC lines, Metcalf-Piercy & Swift, Newark-Dixon Landing upgrade) are no longer sufficient due to load forecast increases. P1, P2, P3, P6 violations on 115 kV paths connecting Metcalf with San Jose B and Monta Vista with Ravenswood. Reconductoring seven 115 kV lines to 1400–3000 Amps addresses existing conductor undersizing (equip_aging).
load_growth_evidence: Objectives explicitly cite 'the aggressive ramp-up in load trends reflected in the current load forecast.' South Bay hosts many AI/data-driven companies. Previously approved projects were re-scoped because load forecast significantly increased since their approval.
alternatives_rejected: • Additional sources into the pocket or expansion of existing substation to prevent overloads. These type of alternatives are not recommended, since this need is already addressed by the bigger scope proposed projects for the area. • Given the high complexity of constructing new transmission assets or upgrading the existing grid in a densely populated urban environment, the lines identified for reconductoring do not have feasible alternatives for comparison. May 30, 2025
interim_solution: Operating solutions such as PST adjustment, HVDC ramp-down, and Los EsterosNortech-NRS 115 kV reactor switching

project_name: Ames Distribution – Palo Alto 115 kV transmission line
brief_description: Construction of a new Ames Distribution – Palo Alto 115 kV line using existing vacant tower positions and idle lines, with a minimum capacity requirement of 1500 Amps, and the expansion of the Ames Distribution and Palo Alto Switching Station buses to allow f or one additional 115 kV connection at each location.
objectives: • Diversifying the sources serving the CPAU load to improve the supply security in the Palo Alto load in case of extreme events like the airplane strikes.
driver_detail: The three 115 kV lines serving the City of Palo Alto share a common corridor near a Santa Clara County General Aviation Airport runway. This corridor 'has experienced two aircraft strikes in recent years.' The primary driver is resilience against extreme infrastructure events (airplane strikes at a shared corridor). The project builds a new Ames Distribution–Palo Alto 115 kV line from a different routing to avoid the common corridor, diversifying supply sources. While P6/P7 thermal violations are also noted starting in 2034, the report specifically highlights the aircraft strike risk as the key justification for the routing.
alternatives_rejected: • New radial line f rom Ames Distribution to a new Adobe Creek substation which will take some of the load of tha Palo Alto station, avoiding the overloads. • New line f rom Ames Distribution to the Adobe Creek station and continuing to Palo Alto. • These alternatives are not recommended because they require a new switching station, which makes them economically unf easible. May 30, 2025

project_name: Metcalf-Piercy & Swift and Newark-Dixon Landing 115 kV Upgrade (re-scope)
brief_description: Reconductor the following 115 kV lines using advanced conductors to achieve a summer emergency rating of 3,000 Amps or higher: Piercy-Metcalf, Swif t-Metcalf , Newark-Dixon Landing, and McKee-Piercy.
objectives: To ensure enough transmission capacity and reliability in one of the most importants 115 kV links between Newark and Metcalf to prevent system overloads due to the aggressive ramp-up in load trends reflected in the current load f orecast
driver_detail: Re-scope of a project originally approved in the 2003 TPP. Objectives explicitly state the cause: 'the aggressive ramp-up in load trends reflected in the current load forecast.' The San Jose area load forecast has increased dramatically since the original project approval, making the originally proposed 795 ACSS reconductoring insufficient. Re-scoped to use advanced conductors achieving 3,000+ Amps summer emergency rating on four lines (Piercy-Metcalf, Swift-Metcalf, Newark-Dixon Landing, McKee-Piercy). Equip_aging: existing line capacity is undersized for projected loads.
load_growth_evidence: Objectives explicitly state 'to prevent system overloads due to the aggressive ramp-up in load trends reflected in the current load forecast.' The project required re-scoping specifically because load forecast increases made the original reconductoring insufficient.

project_name: Sloan Canyon Tertiary Reactors
brief_description: The scope of this project is to install three 66 MVAR shunt reactors on the 24.9 kV tertiary of the Sloan Canyon 500/230 kV transf ormer.
objectives: To address high voltage under contingency conditions. During the P6 contingency the Harry Allen-Sloan Canyon 500 kV and Sloan Canyon-Eldorado 500 kV lines the 500 kV bus voltage at Sloan Canyon was 560 kV in the 2029 summer peak base case which exceeds the 550 kV high voltage limit.
driver_detail: During the P6 contingency (loss of Harry Allen-Sloan Canyon 500 kV and Sloan Canyon-Eldorado 500 kV lines), the 500 kV bus voltage at Sloan Canyon reaches 560 kV, exceeding the 550 kV high-voltage limit in the 2029 summer peak base case. Installing three 66 MVAR shunt reactors on the 24.9 kV tertiary of the Sloan Canyon 500/230 kV transformer provides reactive absorption to control high voltage. This is a re-scope of a previously approved project; analysis of alternatives was conducted when the project was initially proposed.
alternatives_rejected: GLW identif ied the potential f or high voltages with all lines in-service, so deenergizing the lines is not a feasible option due to potential daily operation of the breakers, increased maintenance costs and breaker f ailure rates. No alternatives were considered since this is a project rescope. The analysis of alternatives was conducted when the project was initially proposed.
